disease_label_per_paper: Diffuse brucellar spondylodiscitis due to Brucella melitensis
presentation_summary: 55-year-old woman from Ecuador presented with 3 months of severe lower back pain, bilateral hip pain, left radicular pain, bilateral lower-extremity numbness, tingling, shooting pain, and intermittent fevers.
On presentation she was afebrile with stable vitals and grossly neurologically intact, but pain limited ambulation.
Initial labs showed sodium 123 mmol/L, CRP 5.4 mg/dL, creatinine 0.63 mg/dL, and WBC 5.9 x10^9/L.
Admission MRI showed L5-S1 spondylodiscitis with bilateral epidural, paraspinal, and intramuscular abscesses; the largest abscess was centered in the left piriformis.

Blood cultures grew Brucella melitensis on hospital day 6; biopsy culture from the left gluteal abscess grew Brucella species on day 8. Further history revealed unpasteurized cheese consumption and working with sheep and other livestock.
